clue.text: Sea's energy heading for reef, a lot wiped out

indicators.note: a heading comes at the top, so only the first letter of reef is used
letters that are out are disordered, so the gathered words get rearranged

blocks.note: the heading, or first letter, of reef
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A surfer hits the reef and is wiped out by the ocean's force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wiped out' reads as surfing slang for a fall, but 'wiped' is fodder and 'out' alone signals the rearrangement of R, A LOT and WIPED into TIDAL POWER.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidal power is electricity generated from the rise and fall of the sea, so it is literally energy from the sea.

clue.text: Fashionable model turning the other way

blocks.note: in means in fashion
a model or variant of something is a version

explanation.surface: A trendy fashion model spins round to face the opposite direction.
explanation.definitionFit: An inversion is the act of reversing position or order, a turning upside down or the opposite way.

clue.text: Hackney's hackneyed according to quotation spotted on mug

indicators.note: quoting someone gives their spoken words, here in a Hackney accent, so we go by speech rather than spelling

blocks.note: Hackney is in London's East End, where Cockney speech drops the initial H, so hackneyed comes out as 'ackneyed

explanation.surface: A tired old phrase from Hackney, quoted on a printed mug.
explanation.walkthrough: Mug is slang for face, which turns 'spotted on mug' from a slogan on a cup into a pimply complexion.
explanation.definitionFit: Acned means affected by acne, so a face that is acned is covered in spots.

clue.text: Demure English child revolting when everyone's watching

indicators.note: to revolt is to turn over, so the English child is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: demure and prim both mean modest and proper
standard abbreviation
a little mite is a small child

explanation.surface: A well-behaved English child suddenly misbehaves just when there's an audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolting' looks like the child's behaviour, but it turns the English child round while the demure part stays put.
explanation.definitionFit: Prime time is the evening period of peak television viewing, when the largest audience is tuned in.

clue.text: Opposite sides with row in the middle between spells trouble

indicators.note: only the central character of the word row is wanted
something set between two others sits inside them

blocks.note: west and east are opposite sides of a compass
the middle letter of row

explanation.surface: A quarrel brewing between rival factions in the middle of things means trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: The O goes inside W and E; 'spells' is the link, as in 'this spells trouble'.
explanation.definitionFit: Woe is sorrow or misfortune, a common literary synonym for trouble.

clue.text: Register surfer's opening moves on the waves

indicators.note: an opening is the start, so only the first letter of surfer's is used

blocks.note: a roll is an official list or register
the first letter of surfer's

explanation.surface: Recording the first moves a surfer makes out on the waves.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat rolls when it sways from side to side on the swell, which is how it moves on the waves.

clue.text: Flawed character intrinsic to sporty Polynesians

indicators.note: intrinsic means belonging within, so the letters lie inside the following words

blocks.note: found inside sporTY POlynesians

explanation.surface: A personality defect said to be inherent in athletic Pacific islanders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flawed character' suggests a person's weakness, but character here means a printed letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A typo is a typing or printing mistake, so it is a wrong character on the page.

clue.text: Beefy French dish surfed onto rocks without force

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the letter for force is dropped
something on the rocks is wrecked and broken up, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
F is the symbol for force in physics

explanation.surface: A surfer is dumped onto rocks, though the force seems to have gone out of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tournedos is a French dish of small round beef fillet steaks, so it is a beef-based French recipe.

clue.text: They stand in the surf with boards underfoot

definitions.text: They stand in the surf with boards underfoot

blocks.clueFragment: They stand in the surf with boards underfoot
blocks.note: surface reading: surfers standing in the waves on their surfboards

blocks.clueFragment: They stand in the surf with boards underfoot
blocks.note: cryptic reading: seaside structures built on legs in the water, with wooden planking for a deck

explanation.surface: Surfers standing in the breakers on their boards.
explanation.walkthrough: The boards are not surfboards but the planks of a walkway.
explanation.definitionFit: Piers are platforms on pillars that stretch out into the sea, decked with wooden boards people walk along.

clue.text: Fish attending competition late in the day

blocks.note: an event is a competition at a sports meeting
the ide is a freshwater fish, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: A fish turns up at an angling contest in the late afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: The fish is written after the competition, since it is 'attending' or accompanying it.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventide is a poetic word for evening, the closing part of the day.

clue.text: Bay's attraction pushing learners to the limits

indicators.note: pushing the learners away removes them from where they sit in the word for attraction
limits are the two extremes, so the pushed-out letters are placed at the start and finish

blocks.note: allure is attractiveness or charm
L is a learner driver, so learners are two Ls

explanation.surface: A bay's charm draws novice surfers out to its furthest reaches.
explanation.walkthrough: L is the learner-driver plate, and the learners already sit in the middle of the attraction word; they are moved out, one to each end.
explanation.definitionFit: The bay tree is the sweet bay laurel, whose leaves are used in cooking.

clue.text: Air's foul with daughter rarely having a shower

indicators.note: foul means fouled up or messed about, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written
standard abbreviation in family trees

explanation.surface: The air smells because a daughter seldom washes.
explanation.walkthrough: The shower is rain, not a wash: the surface makes it about personal hygiene.
explanation.definitionFit: An arid place receives very little rain, so it seldom gets a shower of rainfall.

clue.text: Presumably pro now second in finals?

blocks.note: a professional is presumably a former amateur: EX (former) and AM (amateur)
standard abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: Someone who has just turned professional finishing as runner-up in a championship final.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finals' looks like the last rounds of a tournament but means university examinations.
explanation.definitionFit: Finals are the examinations at the end of a degree course, so they are exams.

clue.text: Yankee wears large pants and small socks

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters are treated as a mess to be rearranged
the Yankee is worn by, so placed inside, the reworked letters

blocks.note: taken as written
Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet
standard abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: An American wearing big trousers and tiny socks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' looks like American trousers, matching the Yankee, but works as the British word for rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Argyles are socks knitted in a diamond pattern that originated with the Campbells of Argyll.

clue.text: With this spy might be quietly intrusive

definitions.text: With this spy might be quietly intrusive

indicators.note: read backwards from the result: the quiet letter is the intruder, so taking it out of the spy word gets back to the solution

blocks.note: this reverse clue says the answer with an intruder reads NO SPY, so it opens with NO
taken as written
p is piano, the musical direction to play quietly

explanation.surface: A secret agent who snoops discreetly.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: slip P (quietly) into NOSY and it becomes NO SPY. So NO + SPY with the intruding P removed gives the answer, which itself means intrusive.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone nosy pries into other people's business, which is exactly being intrusive, as a spy is.

clue.text: Land an uppercut, good making connection

blocks.note: an uppercut lands as a hit on the chin
standard abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A boxer lands a good uppercut that really connects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making connection' sounds like a punch landing, but it means coupling things together.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitching is attaching or hooking one thing to another, as when a trailer is coupled to a car.

clue.text: Cold water without risk is boring

blocks.note: C marks the cold water tap
harmless means posing no danger

explanation.surface: Swimming in safe cold water is dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Something charmless lacks any appeal or attraction, so it is dull and boring.

clue.text: Whisky for elevenses? Poor show

blocks.note: elevenses is a mid-morning snack, taken in the AM
a dram is a small measure of whisky

explanation.surface: Drinking whisky at eleven in the morning is a poor show.
explanation.walkthrough: Elevenses is a British mid-morning break for tea and a snack. 'Poor show' sounds like disapproval but means a weak production.
explanation.definitionFit: Am-dram is amateur dramatics, whose performances are proverbially low in quality.

clue.text: Casting off, huge breaks they can't believe

indicators.note: off means out of order or awry, so the letters are rearranged
breaking into something means going inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
OS is short for outsize, a clothing size for huge

explanation.surface: A huge wave breaks over people casting off from the shore, who can't believe it.
explanation.definitionFit: Agnostics hold that God's existence cannot be known, so they cannot commit to belief.

clue.text: Love helping at a party

blocks.note: a do is a party
a ration is a portion or helping

explanation.surface: Someone finds romance while serving food at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoration is deep love and devotion, so it is a stronger synonym for love.

clue.text: Dangerous section of reef, as nutters recalled

indicators.note: a section is a part, so the letters are a run inside the words
to recall is to call back, so the run is read backwards

blocks.note: the letters run across reEF AS NUtters

explanation.surface: A perilous stretch of reef, as crazy surfers remember.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsafe means not safe, which is a straightforward synonym for dangerous.

clue.text: Any number swamped by record break - might one save four?

indicators.note: swamped means engulfed, so the number sits inside the record

blocks.note: a log is a written record
N is any number in maths
a stop is a break or pause

explanation.surface: A wave swamps a record number of surfers, and someone asks who could save four of them.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the long stop is a fielder placed behind the wicketkeeper; four runs are scored if the ball reaches the boundary, which that fielder exists to prevent.
explanation.definitionFit: A long stop is the cricket fielder who stops balls the keeper misses before they run away for four byes.

clue.text: A mega wave

blocks.note: per means a, as in so much per day
M is the symbol for mega, a million

explanation.surface: A huge wave, in surfer's language.
explanation.walkthrough: The surfing theme suggests the sea, but the wave is a hairstyle.
explanation.definitionFit: A perm is a permanent wave, a hairdressing treatment that sets curls into the hair.

clue.text: Fear wiping out's terminal blunder

indicators.note: terminal means at the end, so only the closing letter of out is meant
wiping something out erases it, so that letter is removed from the word for fear

blocks.note: terror is extreme fear
the last letter of out

explanation.surface: A surfer's dread of a final, disastrous wipeout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wiping out' reads as a surfing fall, but 'out's terminal' is the T to be wiped from TERROR.
explanation.definitionFit: An error is a mistake, the everyday synonym for a blunder.

clue.text: Bachelor, one on board, finds footing

indicators.note: on board a ship means within it, so one goes inside the ship's letters

blocks.note: a BA is a Bachelor of Arts
Roman numeral one
SS is steamship, and being on board a ship means within it

explanation.surface: A single man, the only one on a surfboard, keeps his balance.
explanation.walkthrough: The convention is that something 'on board' sits inside SS, the steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: A basis is a foundation, and footing likewise means a firm base something rests on.

clue.text: Turn over a thick plank, possible surfboard material

indicators.note: turning over flips a thing end to end, so it is read backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
a slab is a thick flat piece of wood

explanation.surface: Flip a chunky plank of wood to see whether it could make a surfboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Balsa is a very light wood traditionally used to make surfboards, so it is one possible material for them.

clue.text: Polynesian faces endless ocean with nothing in it

indicators.note: endless means with its end cut off, so the final letter goes
having something in it means holding it inside

blocks.note: the main is a poetic word for the open ocean
zero, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A Pacific islander stares out at the endless, empty sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Faces' looks like a verb but is the plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The moai are the giant carved stone heads of Easter Island, Polynesian faces gazing over the land.

clue.text: Polynesian communist state

blocks.note: Mao Zedong, the Chinese communist leader
RI is Rhode Island, a US state

explanation.surface: A Pacific islander from a communist country.
explanation.definitionFit: The Maori are the Polynesian people of New Zealand.

clue.text: Men on boards in trouble

blocks.note: OR is other ranks, soldiers who are not officers
deal is pine or fir timber cut into boards

explanation.surface: Surfers on their boards get into difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' just places the men before the boards, and 'in' is the link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordeal is a painful or trying experience, a severe form of trouble.

clue.text: Swap ends in very long cricket matches, at intervals

indicators.note: exchanging the end of each word for the other's changes both words' final letters

blocks.note: an epic is very long
ODIs are One Day Internationals in cricket

explanation.surface: The teams change ends during lengthy cricket matches at regular intervals.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the final C and S turns EPIC and ODIS into EPIS and ODIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Episodic means occurring in separate episodes, irregularly and at intervals rather than continuously.

clue.text: Tiller doesn't use hard wood

indicators.note: not using a thing leaves it out, so the hard letter is dropped

blocks.note: a tiller is the bar that steers a boat, the helm
H for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A gardener's tiller works without hard wood.
explanation.walkthrough: Tiller suggests a farmer, but it is the steering bar of a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Elm is a timber from the elm tree, so it is a kind of wood.

clue.text: Golden balls, though that's not all

definitions.text: Golden balls, though that's not all

indicators.note: not having all means the letters of all are taken away

blocks.note: or is gold in heraldry
taken as written

explanation.surface: Golden balls are part of the story, but not the whole of it.
explanation.walkthrough: BALLS without ALL leaves BS. Orbs are balls, and not all orbs are golden, which the clue's tail hints at.
explanation.definitionFit: An orb is a sphere, like the jewelled golden globe carried by a monarch, so orbs are balls.

clue.text: Teacher has said no running around for new students

indicators.note: running suggests movement and disorder, so the letters scatter into a new order
something placed around encloses, so the reworked letters surround the teacher

blocks.note: taken as written
pupils address a female teacher as Miss

explanation.surface: A teacher has refused to let new pupils run around.
explanation.definitionFit: Admissions are people admitted to a school or college, so a year's admissions are its intake of new students.
